name: Joggins Fossil Cliffs
description: Along the Bay of Fundy coast of Nova Scotia, the Joggins Fossil Cliffs stretch for nearly 15 kilometres, and they have been nicknamed the "coal age Galápagos." The eroding cliffs hold fossils from about 300 million years ago, including the footprints of early animals and the stumps of a rainforest, still where they were buried. Strolling the beach at low tide, you can walk through a prehistoric world.
